provenance: All content written for this project; not consulted against R-010 (מאל"ו), R-013 (AnkiWeb), or any NC-licensed dictionary.
source: data/amirnet-vocab.csv (Tier 1, A2) — K-005, alphabetical continuation from "quit" (the next_marker recorded in manifest-2026-09-16-3.json, verified live against the CSV and every existing batch-*.jsonl headword before writing). Ten Tier-1 headwords in this alphabetical span were skipped because a sense already exists in the bank under the same exact headword (range·rate·rather·reach·receive·record·remain·repair·report·return, all from pre-Amirnet NGSL-era batches) — writing them again would not add coverage. "realize/realise" was also skipped: the CSV's slash-variant is already covered by the bare headword "realize" (batch-2026-09-14.jsonl). No other headword in the span quit..remote was skipped.
gate_method: gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) imported directly and run on every row via a temporary script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not pushed — deleted before commit) against the full draft set, using allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt. First-draft level drift (11 of 25 rows flagged on the first pass — background words not in the allow-list, e.g. website/steak/sunlight/politely/lied/Monday/sofa/vacation/app/ten/sunglasses) was fixed with allow-listed replacements (grep -x verified against allowed-words before re-running) and re-verified to 25/25. A negative control (a deliberately broken extra row — Latin letters in translation_he, no Hebrew, a stem with no blank, a stem under the minimum word count, a level outside 1-4, and duplicate/insufficient distractors, several failure axes on the same row) was run through the same checker and correctly rejected before any real row was trusted (0/1 passed). A separate manual scan checked every stem of the form "a ____" for an a/an mismatch with its distractor words (a leak the gate itself does not check) — found and fixed on "quiz" (exam → lesson) and "recent" (elephant → banana), both of which started with a vowel sound after a fixed "a".
distractor_allowed_words_note: Distractor words were not filtered against allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt — the open gap already recorded in manifest-2026-09-16-3.json and earlier manifests (the NGSL-derived pool was built for NGSL-sourced headwords, not the current CEFR-J/Amirnet source; a replacement pool has not been decided or built). gateSense itself does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all.
continuations_regression_note: A second, corpus-level check caught something gateSense cannot see at all: after the 25 rows passed gateSense 25/25, `npm run verify` failed on scripts/measure-continuations.test.ts (order-2 POS-continuation reduction dropped to 19.2%, below the required order1+20=20.1 threshold that K-003's block is reasoned on). Root cause, confirmed by temporarily removing this batch alone and re-running the test (passed 9/9 without it): all 75 item stems (25 words x 3 levels) were written on exactly two fixed syntactic templates (level 2 always "Because X, ...____.", level 3 always "Although X, ...____."), which only recycled POS-trigrams already common in the bank instead of adding novel ones, lowering the engine's block rate. Fix: rewrote 24 of 25 rows' level-2/level-3 stems with varied connectives (since/when/after/while/though/even though) and varied clause order (main-clause-first as well as subordinate-first), re-ran gateSense (25/25, unaffected) and measure-continuations.mjs (order-2 rose to 24.2%), then re-ran the four generators and the full npm run verify (green, including the mobile walk).
batch_size_note: 25 rows, one sense each, full apparatus (2 examples, 3 leveled items, 4 tagged distractors) per row, matching the previous three ticks' scale (14-40). T-353 — which would make sentences/items/distractors optional per Roy's 14/09 volume instruction and let a tick cover many more headwords — is still ⬜ (checked live in plan/50-tasks.md before choosing batch size: no ✅ marker, no closing commit). Until it lands, gateSense/build:ingest/spotCheck still require the full apparatus on every row, so this tick was blocked on T-353 for the volume-only mode and wrote the full-apparatus form instead. 25 was sized to what this tick could hand-author, gate for real (including the a/an manual scan and a negative control), and verify end to end inside the lock window, well under the 1,200-row-per-file ceiling in lib/core/spotCheck.ts.
he_one_to_many_note: Two rows use he_one_to_many_group honestly rather than inventing false precision: "quit" shares its translation_he ("להפסיק") with the existing headword "stop" (batch-2026-08-16.jsonl) — quit implies a more final/complete stopping (a habit, a job), tagged as an interference note. "recent" shares its translation_he ("אחרון") with the existing headword "last" (batch-2026-08-08.jsonl) — Hebrew does not have a single distinct common word for "happened not long ago" versus "final in a series", so both are marked translation_confidence:"medium" with an interference note rather than forcing an artificially precise but inaccurate distinct translation.
next_marker: next alphabetical Tier 1 single-word headword after "remote", not already covered by any existing batch-*.jsonl (checked live against data/amirnet-vocab.csv and all batch-*.jsonl files as of this tick), is "rent" — it is the very next headword alphabetically and was not previously written.
